name: Heavy-duty shears
description: Stout shears with flat, finely serrated blades that bite through armour cloth, tough plastic and thin sheet metal.
notes: 200 mm long, yellow moulded loops, stainless blades lying closed. Id and name avoid the reference's brand name. The reference's butchering is left out: shears are not a butchering tool.

name: Knitting needles
description: A pair of long wooden needles with knobbed ends, for knitting yarn into cloth.
notes: Two 360 mm birch needles, 7 mm thick, walnut knobs. The box counts the gap between the pair (box/volume x3.5).

name: Frame loom
description: A bulky upright wooden frame strung with a warp of threads. Weaving cloth on it is slow, steady work.
notes: Pine frame 0.68 m wide and 0.82 m tall on two feet, a cotton warp, a heddle rod and a strip of striped cloth already woven. CHECK VOLUME (x28) is explained: the frame is open, and the reference's 6 L is the wood alone. It is worked where it stands, so it carries weaving as a workstation only; weaving is a new quality.

name: Bone needle
description: A sharp sliver of bone with a drilled eye. Good enough for rough stitching, but slow and clumsy.
notes: 110 mm long and 7 mm thick, a flat head with an eye slot. sewing 1 as a primitive needle, below a steel needle's 2 and the tailor's kit's 3.

name: Curved needle
description: A half-round steel needle that stitches through one face of a material without piercing the other, as wetsuit seams need.
notes: A half circle 50 mm across. Drawn 3 mm thick, about twice the real wire, so it holds together at the 2 mm grain. sewing 2, a steel needle's grade.

name: Needle
description: A stainless steel sewing needle, long and stout, for mending clothes and making gear.
notes: The reference's 8 g and 1 ml fit a large darning needle, so it is drawn 100 mm long and 3.6 mm thick with a long eye.

name: Wooden needle
description: A whittled wooden needle with a narrow carved eye. Too weak for tough cloth, and slow going on anything else.
notes: 120 mm long and 7 mm thick, pine, with a flat head round the eye.

name: Shed stick
description: A thin, flat wooden stick turned on edge between the warp threads of a loom to open a path for the weft.
notes: 550 mm by 50 mm by 10 mm oak with tapered ends. No tool quality: it is a loom accessory a weaving recipe can name directly.

name: Sewing pattern set
description: A fat envelope of printed paper patterns for cutting out clothing and leather goods. The harder projects need them.
notes: Kraft envelope 310 mm by 230 mm with tissue sheets pulled out at one end, printed lines on them and a shirt outline on the label. pattern_making is a new quality.

name: Tailor's kit
description: A well-stocked sewing case: needles, spools of thread, small shears, an awl and a pincushion. Good for repairing and refitting clothes.
notes: Blue case 180 mm by 110 mm by 30 mm drawn open, lid flat behind. The open lid doubles the footprint (box/volume x2.4). The reference's awl quality maps to punching, the awl quality.

name: Curing hide
description: A treated animal hide rolled up and tied while it cures into leather. Unroll it once it is done.
notes: Roll 260 mm long and 70 mm across, rawhide outside with darker turns at the ends, two jute ties and the loose end lying out. Unrolling when cured needs a timed-transform field the content has not got yet. The loose end widens the box (x2.4).

name: Curing pelt
description: A treated furred pelt rolled up fur side in and tied while it cures. Unroll it once it is done.
notes: Same roll as the curing hide, with fur turns at the ends, fur tufting past them and fur along the loose edge, so the two read apart. Unrolling when cured needs a timed-transform field the content has not got yet. The loose end widens the box (x3).
